q: What is the most abundant element in the Earth’s crust?
e: Oxygen is the most abundant element in the Earth’s crust.

q: What percentage of the atmosphere is made up of oxygen?
e: Oxygen accounts for 21% of the volume of the atmosphere.

q: Which catalyst is used in the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide?
e: Manganese(IV) oxide is used as a catalyst to speed up the reaction.

q: What is the physical state of oxygen at room temperature?
e: Oxygen is a colorless gas at room temperature.

q: What happens when a glowing splinter is placed in oxygen?
e: Oxygen supports combustion and rekindles any glowing thing.

q: What is formed when magnesium reacts with oxygen?
e: Magnesium reacts with oxygen to form magnesium oxide.

q: What is rust?
e: Rust is hydrated iron(II) oxide formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water.

q: Which of the following is an acidic oxide?
e: Carbon dioxide is an acidic oxide that reacts with basic oxides.

q: What type of oxide is zinc oxide?
e: Zinc oxide is an amphoteric oxide, reacting with both acids and alkalis.

q: What is a neutral oxide?
a: An oxide that shows neither acidic nor basic character
An oxide that reacts with acids
An oxide that is soluble in water
e: A neutral oxide does not react with either acids or bases.

q: Which of the following is NOT an allotrope of carbon?
e: Silicon is not an allotrope of carbon; diamond and graphite are.

q: What is the structure of diamond?
e: Diamond has a giant three-dimensional structure with strong carbon-carbon covalent bonds.

q: Why is graphite a good conductor of electricity?
a: It has a high melting point
e: Graphite has free electrons that allow it to conduct electricity.

q: What is fullerene?
a: An allotrope of carbon in the form of a hollow sphere
e: Fullerene is an allotrope of carbon that exists in various shapes including hollow spheres.

q: Which of the following is a property of graphene?
e: Graphene is a transparent and flexible conductor.

q: What is the primary use of charcoal?
e: Charcoal is primarily used as a fuel.

q: What is produced when carbon burns in excess oxygen?
e: When carbon burns in excess oxygen, carbon dioxide is formed.

q: What is the chemical reaction when carbon is used as a reducing agent?
a: Carbon + Zinc oxide -> Zinc + Carbon dioxide
e: Carbon can reduce zinc oxide to zinc and carbon monoxide.

q: What are the amorphous forms of carbon?
e: Coal, charcoal, coke, and carbon black are considered amorphous forms of carbon.

q: What is the main component of coal?
e: Coal contains carbon mixed with compounds of other elements.

q: What does the term 'halogen' mean?
a: A group of highly reactive elements
e: Halogens are highly reactive elements that form diatomic molecules.

q: Which halogen is the most reactive?
e: Fluorine is the most reactive halogen.

q: What is the physical state of bromine at room temperature?
e: Bromine is a liquid at room temperature.

q: What happens when chlorine is passed into a solution of sodium bromide?
e: Chlorine displaces bromine from sodium bromide, forming sodium chloride and liberating bromine.

q: What is the primary use of chlorine in swimming pools?
e: Chlorine is added to swimming pool water to kill bacteria.

q: What is formed when chlorine reacts with water?
e: Chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid and hydrochloric acid.

q: Which halogen is a liquid at room temperature?
e: Bromine is the only halogen that is a liquid at room temperature.

q: What is the property of iodine in the reaction with hydrogen sulfide?
a: It acts as a reducing agent
It acts as an oxidizing agent
e: Iodine acts as a mild oxidizing agent in the reaction with hydrogen sulfide.

q: What type of ions do halogens form?
e: Halogens form anions, known as halide ions.

q: What is the result of adding silver nitrate to a solution containing halide ions?
e: Adding silver nitrate to a solution with halide ions results in the precipitation of silver halides.
